style.vernacular: US-territory Pacific island rebuilt after 1944: low-rise reinforced-concrete and concrete-block buildings (typhoon-proof) in cream, beige and pastel paint with flat or low-pitched roofs, corrugated metal roofs on older houses and shops, big strip malls and car parks, a few coral-stone Spanish colonial remains, hotel towers along Tumon Bay and lush limestone-plateau jungle and palms.
style.ornament: Stylised latte-stone (Chamorro pillar-and-capstone) motifs on civic and airport facades, Spanish colonial coral-stone and lime-mortar masonry in the old town, painted Pacific murals, hurricane shutters and deep overhanging eaves.

sources.what: post-1944 grid streets, several high-rise offices in centre, Plaza de Espana Spanish remains beside the cathedral
before the 1980s redevelopment Spanish-style houses; rebuilt most homes in concrete
stylised latte stone motifs on the terminal front
contemporary design referencing latte stones and local community buildings; beige stucco
